name: Dr. Rong Ge
description: Faculty advisor for Clemson Quantum Club and Ph.D. advisor to Nathan Jones. Teaches Introduction to Quantum Computing (CPSC 4750/6750), Quantum Algorithms and Applications (CPSC 4760/6760), and the Hands‑on Quantum Computing Creative Inquiry (CPSC 3990), which Nathan Jones leads. Research interests include high-performance computing, parallel and distributed systems, and quantum computing education.

name: Dr. Emily Tucker
description: Teaches the Quantum Optimization for Resilient Systems Creative Inquiry (IE 4040), which Jack Layton leads. Research applies stochastic, discrete, and quantum optimization to disaster relief, logistics, and supply chains.

name: Dr. Sumanta Tewari
description: An American Physical Society Fellow whose research focuses on topological quantum computation, Majorana fermions, superconductivity, and condensed matter theory. Teaches Quantum Mechanics I/II (PHYS 4550/4560, 6550/6560, 9510/9520) and Quantum Field Theory (PHYS 9530). His work on semiconductor-superconductor heterostructures helped establish them as a leading platform for Majorana‑based qubits.

name: Dr. Ronnie Chowdhury
description: Eugene Douglas Mays Chair of Transportation in the Glenn Department of Civil Engineering, founding director of the USDOT Center for Connected Multimodal Mobility, and Ph.D. advisor to Valentine Mohaugen. His quantum work applies AI and quantum computing to cybersecurity for transportation and smart-city infrastructure, including the SC Quantum Sentinel initiative. Named a 2024 Clemson University Researcher of the Year.

name: Dr. Ramakrishna Podila
description: Directs the Laboratory of Nano-BioPhysics and teaches Open Quantum Systems (PHYS 8750). His research spans quantum machine learning, nanoscale physics, and nano-bio interfaces, combining condensed matter physics and optical spectroscopy with quantum methods. He is a Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry and the Institute of Physics.
